key_insight: A lightweight EEG deep-learning model (CGA-NSSI) can identify adolescent non-suicidal self-injury while highlighting prefrontal-centered brain network abnormalities.
clinical_relevance: This could support more objective screening of NSSI risk in adolescents alongside interviews and self-report tools, especially where EEG is available.
method: 1D CNN + BiGRU + multi-head self-attention to capture local, long-range, and salient EEG features
Mixup augmentation and Focal Loss to address class imbalance in small clinical datasets
Interpretability plus functional connectivity analysis to link predictions with neurophysiology
evidence_signal: On a real-world adolescent clinical EEG dataset, the model performed well under imbalanced conditions and the analyses showed altered connectivity patterns consistent with NSSI-related neural changes.
watch_item: The findings come from a clinical EEG dataset, so external validation and real-world generalization before deployment remain important.
paper_title: EEG-Based Identification of Adolescent Non-Suicidal Self-Injury and Neurophysiological Interpretation Using an Explainable Deep Learning Framework
